Mar 2025 • Couples

When one is in holiday in the best hotels trust that staff get things right is accepted as derigure. Little was done by the hotel to rectify the situation and so for expedience sake we payed but leave with a very sour taste In our mouth.

AVOID!! Save yourselves the money and you will thank me.

AVERAGE
Jan 2017 • Solo
L'Anmien Restaurant is one of two restaurants located inside Anantara Mui Ne Resort, Phan Thiet City.

I had the opportunity to dine there a couple of nights ago and found the experience to be a mixed bag, although on the whole to be pleasant.

A Thai set dinner promotion was on for VND500,000. But as I was in the mood for western, I decided to look through the menu instead. Unfortunately, the menu was offering mainly Vietnamese and Asian dishes as well. The waitress told me that western food is only offered at the other restaurant within the resort.

In any case, I stuck around and ordered 3 dishes: Lentil Soup; Saffran Lobster; and the Caesar Salad.

The lentil soup was a typical western style cream soup, so I wasn't expecting much from it. However, the kitchen had managed to put their own spin on the soup with some spices, I believe, and it provided a rather good start to my dinner.

The next to arrive was the saffran lobster, which was listed under the appetizer section of the menu. This dish was also beyond my expectation and I found this to be the best of the 3 dishes I ordered. Apparently, the recipe included coconut and curry.

The last dish was the Caesar Salad. Diners can choose to have it chicken or prawns. I selected the latter. Of the 3, I would say this was the most average, perhaps because I was pretty stuffed by then. One thing about this dish - it would be better if the shells were completely removed before serving the dish, see as Caesar Salad was more a western dish than an Asian one. It was also served on a rather small plate that wasn't conducive for me to remove the shell without using my hands. 

For drinks, I had the Coco Mango, a mock-tail. It tasted alright, but not spectacular in anyway whatsoever.

Service wise, there were a couple of hiccups along the way, but nothing major to detract from what was an average dining experience. 

First, the waitress wanted to clear my plate when my fork and knife were still placed on opposite sides of the plate. To be fair, I am not sure if this was due to a lack of training, or because most diners would not know this etiquette and would therefore require the service staff to ask.

The second hiccup occurred during payment. I paid with my credit card, and the staff only gave me a copy of the credit card slip. There was no intention to give me the restaurant receipt until I asked for it. It's quite amazing to me that such a habit still prevails, especially in a 5-star resort.
